verdict: Alphabet's revenue rose 14% to $96.4B as Search and Cloud both grew at double-digit rates — Cloud's operating profit more than doubled — and it kept $28.2B as profit even after a $1.4B legal settlement charge.

segments.name: Google Services
segments.note: Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices. Revenues grew 12%, with Search, subscriptions and YouTube ads all up double digits.

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.note: Cloud computing for businesses — growth of 32% on AI infrastructure and data tools.

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.note: Moonshot projects like Waymo self-driving cars; they lost $1.2B this quarter.

segments.name: Hedging losses
segments.note: Losses on Alphabet's currency-hedging program, which exists to smooth out exchange-rate swings.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers and AI research; up 16% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads and cloud contracts, and marketing Google's products.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back-office, legal and admin costs — including the $1.4B legal settlement charge below.

follow100Note: Google Services is $85.60 of every $100 Alphabet takes in; Cloud adds $14.13. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: A net gain of $2,662M — mainly gains on debt and equity securities Alphabet holds, plus interest income net of interest expense.

takeaways.title: Cloud is compounding
takeaways.text: Google Cloud revenue grew 32% to $13.6B and its operating profit more than doubled to $2.8B — the AI buildout is turning into real earnings, not just sales.

takeaways.title: A legal charge sits in the costs
takeaways.text: General & administrative costs include a $1.4B charge for a settlement in principle of legal matters. Operating income still rose 14% to $31.3B despite it.

takeaways.title: Nearly 30 cents of every dollar became profit
takeaways.text: Net income rose 19% to $28.2B — a 29% margin — even while Alphabet spent $22.4B in the quarter on data centers and other capital projects.

oneTimers: A $1.4 billion charge in general & administrative costs for a settlement in principle of certain legal matters. The charge is not tax-deductible, which also pushed the quarter's tax bill up; without it, operating income would have been $32.7B instead of $31.3B.
